quest.title: Give Her Surprises
quest.description: Sumeru is holding the Sabzeruz Festival! Upon hearing the news, you arrive to see some familiar faces...
quest.rewards_formatted: Primogem x40, Festive Fervor x80, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x4

chapter.num: Chromatic Ode of Candies and Roses: First Gift
chapter.title: Give Her Surprises

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Tighnari and Collei are over there! Oh, and Dehya and Candace are with them!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's go say hi!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Everyone good with their assignment? Then let's get this show on the road.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, and again, please be careful. The last thing we want is for her to find out about our plan.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Don't worry about that! Mercenaries can keep a secret like our lives depend on it.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I'm not sure this scenario is quite that extreme.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: You know what I mean, Candace. It's just a figure of speech.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Um... I'm still kinda nervous. It's not that I'm scared I'll let something slip, it's just... what if she suddenly shows up behind me without warning...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there! What are you guys talking about?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Aaaaaah! Nothing, I swear! I don't know anything you don't know. I'm not hiding anything!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: ...Calm down, Collei. At least check who it is before you freak out.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: #{NICKNAME}! Paimon! Fancy seeing you here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Great to see you all!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Oh, it's you two. Ah... You scared me half to death! Just like when I lose focus in class, and Master Tighnari suddenly shows up behind me, but even scarier!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Are you here for the Sabzeruz Festival?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep! Festivals are always so fun. It seemed like the perfect time to come back and hang out with all of our friends!

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: This one is extra special. I heard from Master that the Akademiya is planning a grand birthday celebration for the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Perhaps it's a small attempt to make amends for their past behavior.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, guess we came at the perfect time! A grand celebration calls for even more good food and fun than usual!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, what were you gossiping about just now? Paimon heard something about a secret?

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Over here, you two. I'll explain everything in private.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: We're preparing a birthday surprise for the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oooh! A Birthday Surprise!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: It was Dehya's idea, actually.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Oh, well... It was just something that occurred to me while talking with Dunyarzad. The Sabzeruz Festival always seems to follow the same formula, so I figured a change of pace might be nice.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Dunyarzad liked the idea, and so did the others. So, we got the ball rolling pretty quickly.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: If we want this to be a surprise, the fewer people who know, the better. We're dealing with the God of Wisdom here — a single slip of the tongue is enough to spoil the whole thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that all makes sense! So, um... do we have to keep talking like this until the festival ends?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Pfft...

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: Ahem! So, anyway, we've only asked a few of our friends to help out, since they happened to have some free time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, what exactly are you planning?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Well, we heard the Dendro Archon loves candy, so we want to take advantage of that.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: We're also planning a birthday meal after the Carriage Parade! So, we'll have a Haft-Mewa Feast as well.

response.speaker: Tighnari
response.text: We left most of the specifics to Kaveh. Right now, all we need to do is purchase the food and decorations.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there anything we can do to help?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, put us to work! Now that we're in on the plan, we should do something to contribute!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey, Candace, weren't you looking for someone to help you with the shopping?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Yeah. I've been in the desert so long, I was worried I wouldn't be the best judge of the goods around here.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We can help with that.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: As long as it's not too much trouble...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No trouble at all! We're more than happy to help!

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey, seems like you're really learning your manners, Paimon.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I'll happily take you up on that offer, then.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Alright, it's settled! Tighnari will book the venue, Dunyarzad and I will take care of decorations, and you three are on food.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahh, so exciting! This is gonna be the best birthday surprise Nahida could ask fo—

response.speaker: Crowd
response.text: Shhh...!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, right! Paimon almost forgot... Gotta keep it a secret...

choices.text: Just tell us. The cat's already out of the bag.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, there's all kinds of delicious scents in the air today! The sea breeze in Port Ormos isn't even enough to cover them up!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: This is the final stop of the Carriage Parade, so many of the vendors decided to set up their stalls in advance. The city is a lot more lively than usual.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: The same goes for Aaru Village. Everyone's doing their part to make this a truly unforgettable Sabzeruz Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, well, with all these vendors, there's no way we're going back empty-handed! Just leave the haggling to us.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Alright, then, let's... Ugh! Ah...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I'm fine...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Sorry for making you worry. Let's go to that store and place an order.

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Welcome! What can I get for you today?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: We'd like to place an order for the Sabzeruz Festival. Could you have them ready for pickup after the parade?

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: No problem at all. What'll it be?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: We'll take three orders each of Masala Cheese Balls, Potato Boats, and Curry Shrimp, and ten orders of Panipuri.

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: One sec, let me jot this down... Potato Boats... Panipuri... Alright, we'll have that ready as scheduled. That's a fairly sizeable order!

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Does that mean we can expect a discount?

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Of course! Let me see... That should come to twenty-nine thousand Mora, but you can have it for twenty-six thousand. How's that sound?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: What about twenty thousand?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Wow... She really went for it.)

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Uhh... That's a bit tricky. We're going to be fairly busy that day, and we're setting aside all these ingredients for your order...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: What if I add five orders of Samosas? Would that help lower the price?

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Well, in that case... the most I can offer is twenty percent off.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Great, we'll take it. Thank you so much.

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Of course! Of course! Thank you for your order.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, it turns out Candace is way better at haggling than us...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Oh, one more thing...

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Something you wanted to add to your order, Miss?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: No. I just wanted to remind you to keep an eye on the fire you've got going there. If you let it burn too long, it could become a safety hazard.

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Oh, thanks for your concern. But, I replaced the charcoal earlier today, so it should be—

response.speaker: Extremely Loud Noise
response.text: BANG!!!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! *cough* There's... so much smoke!

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Ugh... *cough*...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Are you alright?

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: I'm fine, thanks. It's just... That was so strange...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Was it the Wind Generator?

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: *cough*... It's certainly possible. I had a similar problem not too long ago. I thought switching to this one would fix the issue, but...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: We can look into the true cause of the problem a bit later. What matters now is that you're alright. Need any water? I've got some on me.

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: I'm alright! Seems like you've got a good eye, Miss. Just wish your warning came a little earlier. Probably could've avoided this scenario entirely.

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: In any case, I'll definitely fix the stove today, so don't worry about any delays.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Take your time — your health and safety are more important. I'll just leave the deposit here.

response.speaker: Jahangir
response.text: Sounds good. See you soon!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was a close call! Good thing you're fast on your feet, Candace!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you know something was wrong with the stove?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Hmm... I guess you could call it... a gut feeling? It's hard to describe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, where should we go next? Preferably somewhere without any fire hazards. Paimon's still a little traumatized by what happened.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Let's go buy some fruit. We need it to make the candy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds good! It's been a while since we had the chance to shop at Port Ormos. Maybe we can pick up some other things along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's see... The fruit stand should be that way...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Ugh...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Candace? Are you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: ...! Watch out!

dialogues.speaker: Hatice
dialogues.text: ...Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Candace leaps up and saves the child from being hit by a falling crate...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Are you okay, little one?

dialogues.speaker: Hatice
dialogues.text: I... I'm fine! Thank you, Miss!

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That crate came out of nowhere! Luckily, Candace saved that little girl before she got hit.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Where are your parents, child?

dialogues.speaker: Hatice
dialogues.text: Th—They're at the tavern by the harbor, but I got bored, so I came out to play...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: You're safe now, little one. Just be careful next time.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: ...Go back to your parents now, child.

dialogues.speaker: Hatice
dialogues.text: O—Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Whose crates are these?

dialogues.speaker: Kutbi
dialogues.text: Th—They're mine...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: How many times have I told you not to leave heavy objects by the road! When are you going to learn?

dialogues.speaker: Kutbi
dialogues.text: I—I'm sorry! I—It's just... we ran out of storage for our latest shipment...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: And!?

dialogues.speaker: Kutbi
dialogues.text: ...N—Nothing! I'll take care of it right away! I won't do it again!

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone. I should've been keeping a closer eye on everything. Lucky you were here, Miss Candace. I really don't know how things would've turned out, otherwise.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It was nothing. Don't blame yourself, Sheriff. I understand just how difficult it is to look after a whole region. Still, with the festival coming, we need your vigilance more than ever.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: *sigh* Always feels like I could use an extra pair of eyes during Sabzeruz season. I appreciate the reminder, Miss Candace.

dialogues.speaker: Shyam
dialogues.text: Anyway, you were probably in the middle of something, so I'll leave you to it. Enjoy the festival!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was some quick thinking, Candace! It was like you leapt into action before the crate even started to fall.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Like you knew what was gonna happen all along...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Actually, I... I did see something. I saw the crate fall before it happened.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you mean... You saw the future!?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Yes... something similar happened with the stove. I saw what was about to happen...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: I don't think it's related to my amber eye. Growing up, it's never shown me any kind of strange phenomena...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: But, ever since this morning, I've been seeing things that don't match with reality, and after a few seconds, they actually come to pass...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have you told anyone else about this?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Not yet... I still haven't determined if this is the true power of prophecy, and I don't want to make everyone worry.

choices.text: But, why did it come on so suddenly?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Nothing out of the ordinary, really. I prayed to the gods, made my plan for the day, then went to meet my friends.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Although, if I had to think of something... I did buy this gem along the way.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, it's beautiful!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: There's something about it...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: So you sense it, too? This gem seems to contain traces of unusual elemental energy. I only bought it because it piqued my interest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Could the gem be the source of the visions?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: It's certainly possible. Here, try it for yourself. Maybe you'll see something as well...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I don't think anything happened.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Hmm... So, it doesn't work for just anyone.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Perhaps there's some kind of trigger condition... Or could it be because of my connection to Lord Al-Ahmar?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe we could ask the others?

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Everyone's been so busy preparing for the festival. I really don't want to trouble them with something so trivial.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Luckily, I don't have too many responsibilities over the next few days, so I can investigate on my own. It's part of my duty as a "guardian."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We can help too.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Even better! Having your company is like sitting around a bonfire with trusted companions — your presence puts people at ease.

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Alright, let's finish our shopping first, then we can investigate the gem. At the very least, we should ask around the merchant circles for information on its origins.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of merchants... Paimon can think of someone who's always in the know. Although getting information out of her is definitely gonna cost us...

response.speaker: Candace
response.text: Ah, do you mean Dori? I've heard people talk about her in Aaru Village before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yep, that's the one! But, uh, she's pretty touchy when it comes to Mora, so it's best not to haggle too much...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You purchase the fruits on the shopping list...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The vendors tell you where to find Dori.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: ...Here are the goods you asked for, as promised. All of the best quality, I assure you, hehe. Can I interest you in any of my newest offerings before you go?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: No? Well, see you around, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dori!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ohoho! If it isn't two of my most valued customers! And... Miss Candace? Now, this is getting interesting...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What brings the guardian of Aaru village to my neck of the woods? All my business in the desert is strictly above board, I assure you!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: You misunderstand, Miss Dori. We're just here for some information.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ooh! You're in the market for some intel! Well, you've come to the right place! I love dealing in information. It's easy to carry, and even easier to hike up the price! Oh, um... which is always very reasonable of course!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I bought a rather peculiar gem this morning, and I have the name of the merchant who sold it to me.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I want to ask the merchant about the craftsman who cut this gem, and where they got their ore.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ah, so you're looking to track them down? Not an easy job. It'll come at hefty price.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Well, we don't necessarily have to track down that specific person. If you have a way of obtaining the information I seek, Miss Dori, I would be happy to compensate you for those services as well.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (I can find the person no problem, but it's not as lucrative... I have a few connections who work with gemstones, so I'm better off charging them for the information directly.)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, now you're just asking the impossible! These kinds of things tend to be trade secrets. It won't be easy to get that information, even for the great Lord Sangemah Bay.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Just name your price.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Heh, if you insist! Now, let me see... there's the cost of travel, the gifts I'll have to buy...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I'm thinking... around two hundred thousand Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yikes, that's steep!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: That exceeds our budget, I'm afraid. Can you go any lower?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: ...Well, Aaru Village has done me a few favors in the past, so I think we can strike a deal. Why don't you make me an offer.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: How about... fifty thousand Mora?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Excuse me!?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (That's even more aggressive than back at the market...)

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Something wrong? That's usually the going rate for this kind of intel in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Impossible! I wouldn't even be able to put food on the table at that rate! Can't do it, nope!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Ah, what a shame... How about thirty thousand Mora, then?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: That's... That's even lower!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Thirty thousand Mora, plus food, shelter, and a security detail whenever you're in Aaru Village. I'll throw in a few tax exemptions as well. How does that sound?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I—

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Aaru Village certainly has some promising business opportunities... Securing the protection of the local guardian isn't actually a bad trade...)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (Tch... I'm not the only one profiting from this deal, though. I bet she only made that offer so Aaru Village could benefit from more business activity, too... What a scary woman.)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Uh... Hehe... Alright! After some reflection, I've decided to forgo all profit for this venture! Th—Thirty thousand it is!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Ah, now I know why people call you the number one merchant in Sumeru! Your generosity is truly unmatched!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: O—Of course! You're an esteemed client, Miss Candace! I stand more to gain from your friendship than anything else. So, who cares about the Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: If that's the case, then—

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And by that, I mean... we landed on the perfect price! Thirty thousand, as agreed!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: (*sigh*... Just gonna have to treat my gem contact to a 500 Mora food stall instead.)

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I really have to go out of my way to get this intel, so I'll need some time. Why don't you... come back tomorrow!

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Of course. Thank you, Miss Dori. You've been a huge help.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you've only just made it back to Sumeru. Why don't you take some time for yourself? I'll handle the rest of the orders.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? Paimon feels kinda bad, though. We didn't turn out to be much help.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Don't say that. I dragged you into my own personal investigation. I should be the one apologizing.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It was nothing — don't worry about it.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: #Haha, noble as always. May the gods protect you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: And you, Miss Dori. Safe travels. I'll see you tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: *sigh*... Yep. Take care...
